claims.text: The embedding viewer can be searched: type a word, a sentence or a paragraph, or several at once, and the points nearest to each search stay lit while the view keeps moving.

honesty_conditions.text: It holds for real model vectors, not only the synthetic reference: a typed text is embedded by the same model as the data and the lit points are its true nearest neighbours.

claims.text: People who look at their own embedding data in the viewer and want to see what a piece of text links to; hosts that embed the viewer and supply the query embedding; agents that drive the viewer.

honesty_conditions.text: A host can add search with one callback and no build step; a person at the standalone page can search without writing code, given the local helper.

claims.text: The viewer shows a space but cannot be asked anything. To see what a text links to, a person has to find its point by eye.

honesty_conditions.text: It is true today: the shipped viewer has no way to select, highlight or dim points (checked in js/api/50-viewer.md).

claims.text: A search panel under the stage takes one search per line, up to four. Each search becomes a marked point in its own colour; its nearest points stay bright and are joined to it, and the rest of the space dims. A point found by more than one search is shown white. Each pair of searches reports how many points both found and their closest pair of different results.

honesty_conditions.text: Each pair's report is computed from true distances, and a point is white only when it is inside the result radius of two or more searches.

claims.text: It makes retrieval visible: you see what a query retrieves, how far each result truly is, and whether the neighbourhoods of two queries touch.

honesty_conditions.text: What is lit is exactly what a retrieval over the same vectors with the same measure would return, so the picture can be trusted as a retrieval check.

claims.text: Results are the nearest points in the full space, by the stated distance measure, never by position on screen. The view says which measure is used.

honesty_conditions.text: The ranking equals an independent brute-force ranking on the same vectors; on-screen distance is never used for ranking and the page says a projection is a shadow.

claims.instruction: Unit-test the ranking against an independent brute-force computation at 768 and 1024 dimensions.

claims.text: Search never stops or holds the view. A new search swings the view for about six seconds toward the linear view whose first axes join the centres of the searches, while it keeps drifting; then the current mode's own motion carries on with the filter kept. A Face the searches button repeats the swing.

honesty_conditions.text: After any search the frame is still changing every second in every mode; the swing ends by itself and never leaves the view held; reduced-motion and Pause still stop motion as before.

claims.instruction: Measure in a browser that lit pixels keep changing every second during and after a search, in each mode.

claims.text: The filter holds in Tumble, Lattice and Wander, and each keeps its own motion.

honesty_conditions.text: Switching mode with searches active keeps the lit set and the query markers, and Lattice still swaps axes and Wander still flies between points.

claims.text: The search panel takes room only when needed: collapsed by default to one line that names the current searches and how many points are lit; each search's result list is collapsed until opened. The filter stays on while the panel is closed.

honesty_conditions.text: Collapsed, the panel is one line; closing it never clears or pauses the searches; it works by keyboard and states its expanded state to assistive technology.

claims.text: A Distance difference toggle writes each result's true distance on its link and in the list, and how much farther each result is than the nearest one.

honesty_conditions.text: The numbers shown are full-space distances by the stated measure, the same ones used for ranking, not lengths in the picture.

claims.text: A Reranker toggle re-orders the nearest results with a second scorer and says how far each result moved from its embedding order. The toggle appears only when the host supplied a reranker, and the view names the reranker in use.

honesty_conditions.text: With no reranker supplied there is no toggle and no claim of reranking; with one, every result shows its move from embedding order and the reranker is named.

claims.text: A fourth view named Focus: the view is fitted to the results of the search, a ranked list with each result's text sits beside the stage, and clicking a point searches from that point.

honesty_conditions.text: Focus is a separable mode like the other three: adding it changes no existing mode and no part of the data contract; with no search it still shows the whole set.

claims.text: Query embedding is a host callback, embed(text) -> vector. The core file still makes no network request. For local use and the standalone page, embeddings-tumbler viewer serve gains an embed route on its own origin that holds the gateway key in the server process (started under grant run).
The reranker is an optional host callback, rerank(query, candidates) -> scores, offered by the same route as embedding.

The two reference pages are the visual and behavioural reference: docs/specs/reference/tumbler-sky-search.html for search in the three existing views, docs/specs/reference/tumbler-focus-view.html for Focus.
The gateway address and key never reach a page. The core file makes no request; embedding and reranking happen in the host's callback or in the local helper's server process.

honesty_conditions.text: No file shipped to a browser and no response from the local helper contains the gateway address or key; the core file still passes the no-network scan; the helper's embed route answers only its own origin.

claims.text: Linear projections only. The view that faces the searches is a linear projection and the page says so.

honesty_conditions.text: The fitted view is an orthonormal 3-direction frame applied to every point alike; nothing non-linear is introduced, and the status line says the view is fitted to the searches.

claims.text: A query vector whose dimension or model differs from the data shown is refused with a plain message and the view is left unchanged.

honesty_conditions.text: A wrong-dimension or wrong-model vector from the callback never reaches the renderer, and the message names both dimensions or both models.

claims.instruction: Same rule as appends in docs/data-contract.md.

claims.text: The view states, beside the provenance, what a search used: the model that embedded the query, the distance measure, the number of results asked for and the reranker, if any.

honesty_conditions.text: The search line is always visible while a search is active and matches what was actually used; it never names a model the callback did not report.

claims.text: Query text and results are inserted as text, never as markup, and are sent nowhere by the viewer; only the host's callback sees the query.

honesty_conditions.text: A query or result text containing markup creates no element, and the core file makes no request when a search runs (network log shows only the host's own callback traffic).

claims.text: No index: search is an exact scan of the loaded points.
No answer generation and no chat. This shows retrieval; it does not write answers.

On a real data file of 10,000 points, a search lights its results within 1 second of the query vector arriving, and the frame rate with four searches active stays at 30 frames per second or more on the machine used for the earlier measurements.

honesty_conditions.text: The time is measured from the vector arriving to the first frame with the lit set, on the 10,000-point real file, and the frame rate is read over at least 10 seconds with four searches active; the machine and renderer are stated.

claims.instruction: Measure with the browser harness on the 10,000-point Atlas from the real-Atlas proof.

claims.text: With the panel collapsed, search adds at most one line (48 px or less) under the stage.

honesty_conditions.text: Measured in a browser at desktop and phone width with searches active and the panel closed.

claims.text: Clicking a point searches from that point's own vector, so it works without the embed callback.
Every loaded point at least as near as the last named result is lit too, as the sky reference does; results can be asked for from 3 to 20, 8 by default.
Result text is shown when the data file includes text; otherwise the label is shown.

Search among the loaded points is supported as well, with no embedding: by picking a point, or by words matched against the labels and texts already in the data file. It works when the host supplies no embed callback.

honesty_conditions.text: With no embed callback the panel still works and says plainly that it is matching loaded points, not embedding the text; words that match nothing are named, never silently dropped.

claims.instruction: The sky reference does this: a query is placed from the named points its words match.

claims.text: A word search among loaded points places the query at the mean of the matching points' vectors and then lights the nearest points, as the sky reference does; when both are available the panel says which of the two kinds of search ran.

scope_entries.finding: The original reference sky with the filter added: up to four searches, shared points white, a six-second swing to face the searches, collapsed panel. Its vectors are synthetic, so a query is placed from named words; a real build needs a real query vector. The user confirmed this page as the spec on 2026-11-14.

A simpler page: 96 sentences, the view fitted to the results, a ranked list with texts beside the stage, click a point to search from it. The user asked to keep it as an additional view; it is named Focus.

The public API has mount, update, destroy and a handle; nothing selects, highlights or dims points and nothing exposes projected positions. The core file makes no network request of any kind. Search needs new API surface.
viewer serve is static files only, GET and HEAD, and by design reads no environment variable. A local embed route changes that stated property.
Schema v1 has text_included: a file may carry no texts, only labels. Results can show text only when the file has it.
